mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous three months signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) over the previous two months indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals increased economic activity, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% in 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals a tightening monetary policy and inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the previous month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the previous two months signals a weakening in the housing market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST decreases by more than 10% in 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When Real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters, it signals an economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where GDPC1 is negative for two consecutive quarters.
